sources.title: Ulrich Theobald, Southern Qi Dynasty (2011)
sources.note: Indexed original scholarly reference article; direct fetch times out. Used for broad chronology, household registration and document clerks. Do not repeat its inconsistent Xiao Luan death date or claim that Xiao Baojuan died in 502.

sources.title: Audrey G. Spiro, Contemplating the Ancients (1990), chapter 6
sources.note: University of California Press original e-book, indexed full chapter, pp. 122 to 152. Direct page intermittently fails. Search site:pub-ucpec2-prd.cdlib.org "Southern Qi" "molds" "bricks" reproduces relevant text. Three Danyang tombs: only Xiu’anling securely identified by the author; composite décor must not be assigned to one named ruler.

sources.title: Palace Museum, Amitayus stele dated the first year of Yongming (483)
sources.note: Original museum catalogue indexed text. Parallel museum-hosted Forbidden City 2016 issue 10 PDF, printed p. 30: https://www.dpm.org.cn/Uploads/File/2019/07/25/u5d391df0098b4.pdf. Museum object A5541, Sichuan Museum. Modern transcript spells monk Xuansong; PDF OCR mangles his name and measurements, so neither used in copy.

sources.title: Palace Museum, Buddha with two bodhisattvas, Yongming year eight (490)
sources.note: Direct museum text transcribes dated donor inscription; Chengdu Xi’an Road find, Chengdu Museum. Underlying catalogue Sichuan chutu Nanchao Fojiao zaoxiang (2013), pp. 150 to 153, plate 54-1. Related museum PDF u5d391ec884146.pdf printed p. 97 confirms. Public sample uses the catalogue’s simplified-character transcription and our literal English translation, with modern Mandarin reading explicitly distinguished from fifth-century pronunciation.

sources.title: Book of Southern Qi, juan 9: rituals, Chinese Text Project transcription
sources.note: Original Chinese text independently read in indexed result: passage beginning 永明九年正月 for food; numbered paragraph 84 beginning 永明三年正月 for school. 491 and 485 respectively. Ignore the platform’s machine-generated English: copy uses only straightforward Chinese food words and the explicit 200 students. Later compiled dynastic history, not original fifth-century edict artifact.

sources.title: Michael Stanley-Baker and Shih-Pei Chen, Mapping Drugs in Early Medieval China, Max Planck Institute
sources.note: Direct research project text quotes Tao Hongjing’s Bencao jing jizhu preface, dated 492 to 498. Describes supply chain, identification and adulteration as historical issues, not evidence for modern therapeutic efficacy.

sources.title: Meow Hui Goh, Sound and Sight: Poetry and Courtier Culture in the Yongming Era (483 to 493), 2010
sources.note: Original publisher description read through indexed text; direct fetch unavailable. Book description supports sensory poetry and Buddhist interpretation, not specific invented poem dates. Author’s university research description corroborates Shen Yue, Wang Rong and Xie Tiao: https://china.usc.edu/event/meow-hui-goh-generational-remembrance-and-forgetting-late-han-chaos-cao-courts .

sources.title: Biographical Encyclopedia of Astronomers, Zu Chongzhi (2007), University of St Andrews copy
sources.note: Direct three-page entry, pp. 1 to 2. Explicit service under Liu Song and Southern Qi; 462 proposed calendar, 510 adoption, son Zu Geng’s role, shadow observations and pi interval. Does not date every mathematical result to Southern Qi.

proposedOverrides.name: Southern Qi
proposedOverrides.summary: A short-lived southern Chinese dynasty centred on Jiankang, with influential court poetry, Buddhist patronage and medical scholarship.

batchIdentityNotes.note: Exact curated index 479 to 502, but imported TopoJSON exists only 500 to 502. Bbox 99.7516,17.6647 to 122.3922,37.9498; Jiankang, Danyang and Chengdu included, Luoyang and Ye excluded. Coarse outline caveat public; no unsupported precise boundary correction. Preserve existing curated fell year502 to liang-dynasty, omitted from override. No aliases to Northern Qi, Liu Song, Liang or Chen. Primary text school/food translation is our reading of Chinese, not CText AI English. Two Palace Museum entries conservatively combined as the same underlying 2013 catalogue for budget purposes.
